criteria.live_only: Expose caret exclusively through paired live calls: read_selection(node) returns the current selection record and set_selection(node, start, end, direction) writes it. Event snapshots carry no caret field, so handlers that need the caret issue an explicit read; snapshots stay smaller at the cost of an extra call per caret-aware handler.
criteria.snapshot_only: Project caret into every event snapshot as a nested selection record with start, end and direction, and add a set_selection(node, start, end, direction) live setter. Offer no live caret read: handlers observe the caret from the dispatch-time snapshot and restore it with the setter, keeping the read surface minimal.
criteria.symmetric_calls: Project caret into event snapshots as a nested selection record and provide both read_selection(node) and set_selection(node, start, end, direction) live calls, so caret is observable at dispatch and re-readable later (save-time, focus repair, async continuations) with one symmetric read/write pair.

caret_projection.instructions: Which caret and text-selection projection should the Can browser boundary adopt for normalization and focus repair?

criteria.flag_only: Add a composing boolean holding the native isComposing flag to input and key snapshots, and admit no new event kinds. Can handlers defer normalization while composing is true and derive composition transitions from consecutive input events.
criteria.flag_plus_end: Add the composing boolean to existing snapshots and additionally admit the compositionend event kind only, giving handlers an explicit commit signal alongside the flag without the full start/update vocabulary.
criteria.new_kinds: Admit compositionstart, compositionupdate and compositionend as new event kinds, with snapshots carrying the composing boolean plus a data string holding native event.data. Input events also carry the flag, so both transition-driven and flag-driven handlers work.

composition_signal.instructions: How should IME composition state reach Can event handlers?

criteria.metadata_records: Snapshot chosen files as an array of file records with name, size and mime fields on change events, plus a read_files(node) live call returning the same shape. Cap the projection at the first 128 entries in selection order with the bound documented; file bytes never cross the boundary.
criteria.names_only: Snapshot chosen files as a plain string array of file names, with read_files(node) returning names live. Size and mime stay unavailable, keeping the projection minimal at the cost of size/type validation before upload.
criteria.opaque_handles: Snapshot chosen files as opaque file-handle tokens with a read_file_metadata(handle) call returning name, size and mime. Handles reserve a future upload path while metadata stays behind an explicit call; no upload consumer exists yet.

file_projection.instructions: Which file-input selection projection should the Can browser boundary adopt?

criteria.chord_string: Carry modifiers as one sorted chord string on the event, joining held modifiers with '+' in alt, ctrl, meta, shift order ('', 'ctrl', 'ctrl+shift'). One compact field at the cost of string parsing for per-modifier tests.
criteria.flat_bools: Carry four booleans directly on the event record (alt_key, ctrl_key, meta_key, shift_key). No new catalogue type, but four more top-level snapshot fields.
criteria.nested_record: Carry modifiers as one nested modifiers record with alt, ctrl, meta and shift boolean fields. One new catalogue type and one new event field, with per-modifier tests as plain field reads.

modifier_shape.instructions: Which modifier-key projection shape should browser event snapshots use?

state.boundary: The Can browser boundary at 27338b09 snapshots exactly four event fields (kind, target, value, key) and admits nine event kinds: click, dblclick, input, change, keydown, keyup, focus, blur, submit. Writes are attribute-only: setAttribute changes the default while a dirty live input value keeps user text (probed). Checked and unchecked checkbox change events yield identical snapshots with value 'on' (probed). No caret, modifier, composition, multiselect or file projection exists, and no live value or checked setter exists.
state.contract: R02 interface C-D requires each addition to ship as a catalogue plus checker plus adapter slice with a bounded immutable projection: snapshots are immutable records captured synchronously at dispatch, live setters take explicit values, and selection or caret operations are explicit calls. Snapshot evolution is additive only: the four existing fields keep their exact meaning. Returned collections are fresh copies with no mutable escape. View-scoped listener lifetimes and disposal semantics stay unchanged. Zero external users exist, so no legacy compatibility burden applies beyond the selected additive contract.
state.evidence: Each addition ships native-DOM plus emitted-Can legs in Chromium 140.0.7339.186, WebKit 26.0 and Firefox 141.0 (container runner), covering dirty value and checked reset, autofill observation, per-field projection checks, no-mutable-escape checks, and the preserved existing snapshot legs.
state.fixed: Already decided and outside this consultation: checked boolean and selected string-array snapshot fields; set_value, set_checked and set_selected live setters; read_value, read_checked, read_selected and read_files live reads. Open here: caret projection (snapshot versus live calls), file projection shape, modifier-key shape, and the IME composition signal.
state.workflows: The all-Can workflows the additions must serve: input normalization preserving caret; dirty value and checked reset to defaults; autofill observation; multiselect choose, read and reset; file-upload selection reads; IME composition with deferred normalization; focus and caret repair across rerender; shift+click range selection in the keyed table; row reorder; independent view disposal; and late replies that never clobber newer edits.
